world_geopolitics_misc.title: Which European country will announce plans to shut down its only nuclear power plant because of drought-related cooling-water shortages by August 2, 2026?
world_geopolitics_misc.background: Nuclear power plants that use river water for cooling can face operational restrictions when drought reduces the available water supply.
world_geopolitics_misc.resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Official government statements or contemporaneous reporting by established news organizations.
  • Resolution Rule: Identify the European country whose government announces, between July 1 and August 2, 2026, inclusive, plans for a complete shutdown of its sole operating nuclear power plant because drought has reduced the river water available for reactor cooling. The announcement of the shutdown plan is sufficient; the shutdown itself need not have occurred. A partial reduction in electricity output alone does not qualify.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The country's commonly used English name.

current_state.key_facts: July 23 UPDATE (Romania Insider July 17, Reuters/Straits Times July 20 & July 21): Major hydrological escalation centered on Romania and the Lower Danube! On July 16-19, Danube flow at Bazias (entry into Romania) plunged to 1,700-1,750 m3/s (lowest in 30 years vs 4,700 m3/s July norm), explicitly compared by Romanian Waters to the August 2003 minimum (1,650 m3/s) that forced Cernavoda to shut down. Authorities imposed Level III irrigation restrictions on the Calarasi-Cernavoda stretch and began emergency controlled releases from Olt and Arges hydropower reservoirs specifically to maintain minimum cooling water levels for Nuclearelectrica's two Cernavoda reactors. Although Romania hoped rains from July 20 would nudge flow up modestly (~1,900 m3/s, still 60% below normal), Reuters reported on July 21 that Danube levels in Serbia (directly upstream of Romania & Bulgaria) hit their lowest since 1946, also disrupting the Sava river. Updated: Romania 0.39->0.54 (strongest physical cooling-water shortage evidence, capped <0.60 as reservoir mitigation is active and no shutdown announced yet), Slovenia 0.27->0.19 (single-reactor Krsko + Sava low in Serbia, but cooling towers & no Krsko emergency reported), Bulgaria 0.14->0.16 (shares Lower Danube crisis downstream of Serbia 1946-low at Kozloduy), Hungary 0.17->0.09 (4 reactors ~50% of grid + July 1 thermal exemption), Belarus 0.02->0.01. Sum = 0.99.
current_state.next_review_trigger: Check daily July 24-30 for Danube water level at Cernavoda/Kozloduy (watch 2.50/2.35 mdMB thresholds), Sava/Krsko status, or official shutdown plan announcement.

mixed_1.title: In which country outside Iran, if any, will US forces strike Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026?
mixed_1.background: Iran-aligned armed groups operate across several Middle Eastern countries, creating potential flashpoints for military confrontation with the United States.
mixed_1.resolution_criteria:
• Source of Truth: Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera, supported where available by official military statements.
  • Resolution Conditions: Identify the country outside Iran where US forces conduct strikes against Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026, inclusive. Direct US participation in either unilateral or joint strikes qualifies; threats, proposed operations, and diplomatic support do not.
  • Accepted Answer Format: The country's name, or “None” if no qualifying strikes occur.
